note: EXPERIMENT 2: is rank just another strength knob, or does it carry independent directional content? The paradox to explain: at lr 1e-4 on this stream r128 fits harder (mean delta_in 31.1% vs 11.9%) and transfers more to adjacent chunks (V1-A T 1.27% vs 0.61%), yet its full-stream gain is far worse (4.09% vs 9.94%). If rank were purely a strength knob, r128 run at a lower lr - so that its realised strength (mean delta_in) matches r32 - should land on the SAME point of the delta_in -> delta_pct curve. Read on the (delta_in, delta_pct) plane via collapse_curve.py: r128 ON the r32 curve = rank is pure strength, the direction-correction premise dies (just tune lr). r128 BELOW the curve at matched delta_in = the extra directions are actively harmful, so there is something to fix. r128 ABOVE = extra directions help and matched strength is all you need. Reuses the existing gk_mixed points at lr 1e-4, so only the other three lrs are swept here. measure_gk is what supplies mean delta_in. lr 3e-4 may diverge at r128; that is informative and collapse_curve marks it. lora_r is in the grid -> alpha=2*r.
